$comment: P68 round 9 (lane `cs`) — an INDEX DESIGNATOR is compared with its array's bound at FULL width (negative / diagnostic). C 6.7.9p6: a designator `[ constant-expression ]` of an array of known size must name one of its elements. Both of DSS's tiers narrowed the index to 32 bits before asking, so an index of 2^32 or more WRAPPED to a small in-range one and the element was stored there SILENTLY — `int a[2] = {[4294967296] = 7}` ran 7 out of a[0]. The placement cursor now takes the index at full width and owns the one check. MEASURED 2026-09-23, this file compiled on each reference separately: gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 at -std=c17 -pedantic-errors and -std=c2x, and mingw-w64 13.2.0 at both, refuse it ('array index in initializer exceeds array bounds' / 'array designator index (4294967296) exceeds array bounds (2)'); MSVC 19.51 at /std:c17 and /std:clatest refuses it (C2078) — it builds the NESTED shape alone while dropping its value (the lane's `.temp/probe/dx` d04 ran 0), which is no semantics to follow. The same shapes IN range, in `accepted`, draw nothing, and the expectation is EXACT SET EQUALITY, so a check that refused every designated element would red this entry as surely as one that refused none. RED-ON-DISABLE: the cursor comparing only the low 32 bits of an index, or either tier narrowing it again -> these five refusals vanish and the build succeeds.
